talking_points.headline: AI concentration is now embedded across every asset class, breaking Wall Street's diversification playbook
talking_points.context_html: Lisa Shalett, Chief Investment Officer of Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, warns that AI exposure has spread so widely — Goldman Sachs puts AI-linked firms at 40% of S&P 500 market cap, Apollo finds AI-related bonds near half of investment-grade issuance — that classic diversification no longer protects client portfolios. The $327bn New York City Retirement Systems has already begun declining private-equity funds on AI over-concentration grounds. For Adam, this is a live product-risk and advisory-conversation problem: HSBC's investment counsellors and RMs need a credible, differentiated answer when UHNW clients ask whether their 'balanced' portfolio is secretly one large correlated AI bet.
source_links: AI Boom Is Making Diversifying Investments Tough

talking_points.headline: Banks want AI trade surveillance everywhere; almost none have the data to run it
talking_points.context_html: A new 1LoD industry survey finds 89% of banks want AI-enhanced trade surveillance but only 11% have it live, and pins 71% of the gap on data quality rather than budget or regulatory caution. That is exactly the constraint sitting under HSBC's own AI ambitions, from the Google Cloud partnership to Wealth Intelligence: the industry-wide evidence says the binding constraint on scaling AI is upstream data governance, not model capability or spend. For Adam, it reframes the change-execution agenda — the next AI win depends less on picking the right model and more on winning the unglamorous data-remediation fight first.
source_links: Banks Want AI Surveillance But Lack Data

Private Banking & Wealth.title: AI Boom Is Making Diversifying Investments Tough for Wall Street
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Goldman Sachs data shows AI-linked firms now make up 40% of S&P 500 market cap and Apollo finds AI-related bonds are near half of investment-grade issuance, meaning AI exposure now runs through equities, credit and private markets alike. The $327bn New York City Retirement Systems has already declined a private-equity fund over-concentrated in AI, and Morgan Stanley Wealth Management CIO Lisa Shalett warns that classic diversification no longer shields portfolios from a single correlated bet. For HSBC WPB this is a live advisory-conversation risk: RMs and investment counsellors need a credible answer when UHNW clients ask whether their 'diversified' book is quietly one large AI trade.

AI & Technology.title: Banks Want AI Surveillance But Lack the Data to Run It
AI & Technology.summary: The 1LoD 2026 Surveillance Benchmarking Survey finds 89% of banks want AI-enhanced trade surveillance but only 11% have deployed it, and 78% want generative-AI assistants for analysts against just 7% actually live, with 71% of respondents tracing the gap to data quality — fragmented silos and inconsistent formats — rather than budget or regulatory caution. That is precisely the constraint sitting under HSBC's own AI ambitions, from the Google Cloud partnership to Wealth Intelligence: the industry-wide evidence says the binding constraint on scaling AI is upstream data governance, not model capability or spend. For Adam this reframes the change-execution agenda: the next AI win depends less on picking the right model and more on winning the unglamorous data-remediation fight first.
